answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards, with slashing triggered by provable double-spending or collusion across a thread of tasks. The stake does not prove a human identity; it makes mass identities expensive and exposes capital to loss when misconduct is evidenced. An attacker must tie up real resources for every Sybil, risking forfeiture, while honest agents can harbor reputation across tasks. Even an umber-colored avatar gets no cheaper entry.
